evals.prompt: I'm building an order processing system in Go. Orders are produced by a web API and need to be processed by exactly one of several worker instances, with retries on failure. Show me how to model the stream and consumer in JetStream and write the producer plus a worker.
evals.expected_output: WorkQueue stream + durable pull consumer with explicit ack, MaxDeliver retries, idempotent publish (Nats-Msg-Id), and correct modular @nats-io or Go nats.go usage.

assertions.text: Uses a WorkQueue-retention stream
Consumer uses explicit ack (AckExplicit)
Sets MaxDeliver to bound retries
Publisher sets Nats-Msg-Id for idempotent/dedup publish
Uses a durable PULL consumer (not push/ephemeral)

evals.prompt: I need to deploy a 3-node NATS JetStream cluster on Kubernetes. We're running production workloads and need file storage that survives pod restarts. Give me the Helm values or manifests and explain the sizing.
evals.expected_output: 3-replica StatefulSet/Helm with JetStream file storage on a PVC, anti-affinity, pinned (non-latest) image, resource sizing guidance.

assertions.text: Declares 3 replicas (StatefulSet or Helm cluster size 3)
JetStream file storage backed by a PersistentVolumeClaim
Pins a specific NATS image tag (not 'latest')
Includes pod anti-affinity to spread across nodes
Provides resource/disk sizing guidance

evals.prompt: My JetStream consumer has been falling behind for the past hour. nats consumer report shows Num Pending climbing and Num Ack Pending pinned at the max. Walk me through diagnosing and fixing it.
evals.expected_output: Identifies MaxAckPending saturation / slow consumers / AckWait redelivery, uses nats consumer report/info, gives concrete edit commands and prevention.

assertions.text: Identifies MaxAckPending saturation as a root cause
Uses nats consumer report/info to diagnose
Addresses AckWait-driven redelivery
Gives concrete remediation commands (max-pending / workers / batch)

evals.prompt: Using the Synadia agents SDK in TypeScript, build a meta-agent that discovers the other AI agents registered over NATS and fans a single prompt out to all of them, then merges their replies. Show the discovery and the fan-out.
evals.expected_output: Uses @synadia-ai/agents, discovers agents (e.g. $SRV/agents.* or SDK discovery), fans a prompt to each, merges streamed replies; protocol-compliant subjects.

assertions.text: Imports the @synadia-ai/agents SDK
Performs agent discovery over NATS
Fans the prompt out to multiple discovered agents
Merges/aggregates the agent replies
Uses protocol-compliant agents.* / $SRV subjects

evals.prompt: We're running NATS server 2.11 in production. I want atomic batch publishing (all-or-nothing writes of a group of messages) and per-message TTL on my streams, in Go. Set it up.
evals.expected_output: Flags that atomic batch publish needs server 2.12 (api.level 2) + allow_atomic, so 2.11 cannot do it; per-message TTL works on 2.11 but requires allow_msg_ttl on the stream; recommends capability detection via api.level rather than assuming.

assertions.text: States atomic batch publishing requires server 2.12+ (NOT available on 2.11)
Does not present atomic batch as working on 2.11
Per-message TTL requires allow_msg_ttl on the stream
Recommends capability detection via api.level

evals.prompt: Set up a dead-letter queue in NATS JetStream: when a message in my work queue fails processing 5 times, it should go to a DLQ so I can inspect and replay it. Go.
evals.expected_output: States NATS has no native DLQ; builds it with MaxDeliver=5 plus a consumer of the $JS.EVENT.ADVISORY.*.MAX_DELIVERIES advisory that republishes/copies the exhausted message to a separate DLQ stream; notes the message is not auto-deleted.

assertions.text: States NATS has no native dead-letter queue
Uses MaxDeliver=5 to bound retries
Consumes the MAX_DELIVERIES advisory to catch exhausted messages
Republishes/copies the failed message to a separate DLQ stream
Notes the original message is not auto-deleted from the stream
